forecastReasoning.narrative:
Warm-Front Wave governs the 12Z Day 1–12Z Day 2 period. The 12Z Day 1 issuance carries a MDT maximum, with Slight-or-greater probabilities covering 32% of the domain. The primary corridor peaks near 15Z Day 1, when mean initiation reaches 5% and expected storm coverage reaches 3%.

A baroclinic warm front focuses moisture pooling, backed low-level flow, and repeated ascent. A representative corridor sounding contains about 3861 J/kg CAPE, 383 m²/s² SRH, 68 kt deep-layer shear, 1658 m LCLs, STP 7.5, and VTP 2.4. Flow increases from roughly 34 kt at 850 mb to 46 kt at 500 mb and 58 kt at 250 mb.

Maximum probabilities are 15% tornado, 0% hail, and 0% wind; tornadoes is the leading hazard signal. The analog ensemble has high agreement (94% confidence; 30 members), with mean moisture return 91%, clearing 61%, forcing 89%, and cap persistence 31%. No ensemble failure mode exceeds the reporting threshold.

Rich boundary-layer moisture (66°F representative dewpoint)
Strong buoyancy (3861 J/kg CAPE)
Weak inhibition (41 J/kg CIN)
Strong deep-layer shear (68 kt)
Strong low-level hodograph curvature (383 m²/s² SRH)
Storm mode and conditional intensity support tornado potential
limitingFactors: Low or highly localized initiation signal (5% corridor mean)
Sparse expected storm coverage (3% corridor mean)
